transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (CTO, Hypernova), Marta Gomez (Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy): Hypernova looking for integration patterns, single gateway, per-tenant quotas, want hosted for POC but Private/Dedicated for customers requiring data residency. Ask for LangChain/Llamaindex examples and observability/tracing hooks into their existing Splunk stack.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Ava AE on the account, Ethan and Priya from our SE team with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Ravi: Good, hey Ava, thanks. Busy week but excited to chat, we just started scoping LLM features across three product teams.
[00:14] Marta: Hi all. We mainly use a transformer-based pipeline in house and are trying to consolidate inference.
[00:20] Ethan: Nice, maybe start with a quick goal check — what do you want from Redwood? Is it latency, multi-tenancy cost savings, private deployments?
[00:32] Ravi: All of it, really. For the POC we want fast integration, so hosted is attractive, but for regulated customers we need VPC or on-prem later. Also we want a single gateway in front of multiple models and backends.
[00:45] Priya: When you say gateway, do you mean a proxy that normalizes auth and routing, or more of an API gateway with per-tenant quotas?
[00:53] Liam: Both. We have multi-tenant SaaS so we'd like a single upstream endpoint that does token translation, per-tenant rate limiting and routes to Dedicated pools or Hosted fallback.
[01:08] Ethan: That's a common pattern. Redwood supports that: you can run a lightweight gateway we recommend, or use your existing API gateway like Kong/Envoy and call Redwood endpoints. We also have a gateway example repo that shows JWT translation to Redwood API key, per-tenant header mapping, and route-based model selection.
[01:28] Marta: Do you have examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex integration? Our ML folks build retrieval-augmented pipelines using LlamaIndex.
[01:35] Ethan: Yes — we have SDKs in Python/JS and dedicated examples for LangChain/LLamaIndex. The LangChain example shows an LLM wrapper using Redwood's streaming responses and connectors for embeddings. There's a small mismatch sometimes where LlamaIndex wants direct control of cache/KV — our SDK exposes the KV/cache hooks but docs can be terse. We'll share a repo.
[01:56] Ravi: What about model pinning and rollouts? We need to pin used model versions per tenant during a canary.
[02:03] Priya: Redwood supports model version pinning and rollout policies. You can configure canaries and automatic fallbacks if capacity is constrained. For Dedicated customers you get pool-level isolation so you can guarantee throughput.
[02:16] Liam: Can the gateway decide to route to Hosted but fall back to Dedicated, or vice versa? We want cost-driven routing.
[02:23] Ethan: Yes, routing can be policy-driven. You can annotate requests with tenant id, cost tier, or latency SLO and route accordingly. We also support automatic fallback to a cheaper/compatible model when a primary is unavailable.
[02:36] Marta: Observability is huge for us. We use Splunk and also want request traces tied back to our spans. Any hooks?
[02:44] Priya: We provide tracing headers you can propagate; when you enable tracing Redwood surfaces per-request timing in the console. You can also push logs to your logging endpoint, and we expose token-level breakdowns and per-route latency.
[02:58] Ravi: Any out-of-the-box integration for OpenTelemetry?
[03:02] Ethan: We ingest OpenTelemetry traces via a collector — we have docs and a sample collector config. It does require a small sidecar or forwarding from your tracing collector to Redwood observability endpoint.
[03:19] Liam: On quotas, we want per-tenant monthly quotas plus burst tokens. How granular are your quotas?
[03:26] Priya: You can set per-key and per-tenant quotas, with burst windows. Quotas are enforced at the edge and we support rate-limits per second and per minute plus monthly consumption accounting. We also expose webhook alerts when thresholds approach.
[03:42] Marta: Is there throttling behavior on streaming responses if quotas are exceeded mid-stream? We have streaming chat UIs.
[03:50] Ethan: If quota is exhausted mid-stream the stream will close with a quota-exceeded code and a structured error. You can configure graceful degradation to a cheaper model or cached response instead of hard cut-off.
[04:05] Ravi: About security — SSO, RBAC, KMS, audit logs — our legal/security team will want details.
[04:12] Priya: We have SAML SSO, RBAC in the console, full audit logs, and KMS integrations for Private deployments. For Hosted we provide encryption at-rest and in-transit; for Dedicated/Private we can integrate customer KMS. We'll send the security whitepaper.
[04:30] Ava: We'll attach our SOC2 docs and the Private deployment checklist after the call.
[04:35] Ravi: Great. For the gateway pattern — can you show a simple flow you're recommending?
[04:40] Ethan: Sure — typical pattern: clients -> Hypernova gateway (auth, tenant lookup, per-tenant quotas) -> Redwood endpoint(s). Gateway adds tenant-id and trace headers and chooses model route. For latency-sensitive traffic we route to a dedicated pool; for low-priority we route to hosted.
[05:02] Marta: How do you handle embeddings? We have a separate embedding pipeline — do you prefer a single endpoint for both embeddings and generation?
[05:10] Priya: We recommend separate routes so you can tune batching/latency differently, but a single gateway can expose both under different paths; Embeddings usually have different token accounting/throughput profiles.
[05:22] Liam: Do we need to manage batching ourselves or can Redwood handle it downstream?
[05:27] Ethan: Redwood runtime does continuous batching and kernel selection server-side, but we also provide client-side batching libraries in the SDK for better efficiency in high-throughput scenarios. For embeddings, batching client-side often improves throughput and cost.
[05:44] Ravi: For the POC timeline, we want to show a working integration in two weeks. Would that be feasible?
[05:50] Ava: Yes, two weeks for a POC connecting a gateway, basic auth, and doing a few prompts/benchmarks is a typical timeline. We'll provide examples and a sandbox hosted project to speed things up.
[06:01] Marta: Can you share concrete LangChain snippet? I sometimes see differences in the LLM wrapper interface across providers.
[06:08] Ethan: Example: in Python you can wrap Redwood via our LangChain LLM wrapper: RedwoodLLM(api_key=..., model_name=... , streaming=True). For LlamaIndex you can use RedwoodEmbeddings and pass the embedding function to the index builder. We'll push code that specifically handles streaming chunk merging — docs have a note about chunked tokens being labeled differently so need small adapt.
[06:34] Liam: A question about private deployment networking: if we go with Private, what's required for peering? Do you do VPC peering or reverse tunnel?
[06:41] Priya: We support both models depending on your security posture. For VPC peering we need CIDR ranges, firewall rules, and optionally AWS Transit setup. For air-gapped on-prem we do an appliance with HSM/KMS integration. We'll follow up with a network checklist.
[06:57] Ravi: Benchmarks: we want to run our three prompts against your hosted and dedicated pools and see per-token latency and cost. Can you run those?
[07:06] Ethan: Absolutely — if you give us prompts and expected concurrency we'll spin up a dedicated pool for benchmark or use hosted and record results. For Dedicated we'll attach the exact GPU type and config in the report.
[07:18] Marta: A slightly weird ask — can Redwood return structured output or function call style responses? We use structured JSON results.
[07:26] Priya: Yes, we support structured output and function/tool calling patterns. The SDK has helpers to validate schema and we can surface parsing errors in the console.
[07:36] Ravi: Any limitations with LlamaIndex? We use a lot of custom nodes and indexes.
[07:40] Ethan: Noted — LlamaIndex is supported but there are occasional nuances with streaming and index-level caching. We have an example where you offload some cache to Redis and use the SDK's KV hooks to keep cache coherent. It's in the repo we'll send.
[07:58] Ava: I'm going to recap real quick. Items: we'll send pricing and SOW, SEs will post code samples and gateway repo, Hypernova will send prompts, and we'll schedule infra deep-dive. Does that cover it?
[08:10] Ravi: Yes, that's perfect. One more thing — quota billing: is usage billed per-tenant or per-account?
[08:17] Priya: On Hosted it's per-account keys but we support metering per-tenant via usage tags and can optionally surface separate invoices via billing exports. For Dedicated/Private you get more flexible metering.
[08:31] Marta: Regarding failure modes — if Dedicated pool is saturated, how fast is fallback to hosted? Is that a manual or automatic switch?
[08:40] Ethan: You can configure automatic fallback policies; fallback latency is sub-second for routing decisions but of course provisioning capacity takes longer. For sustained overload we recommend autoscaling or reserved burst pool.
[08:55] Liam: About rate-limits we need deterministic throttling for some customers (SLA). How do you guarantee that?
[09:02] Priya: For strict SLAs we recommend Dedicated with pool isolation and guaranteed QPS. For hosted we offer best-effort quotas; for deterministic behavior Dedicated is the way.
[09:15] Ravi: Any compliance artifacts you can share now?
[09:18] Ava: I'll attach SOC2, DPIA, and our Private deployment security checklist in an email following this meeting.
[09:24] Marta: Great. Next step: sending repo and sample code will help developers start in parallel.
[09:30] Ethan: We'll also include a mini gateway Docker image and an Envoy filter example for header translation and JWT to API key mapping.
[09:39] Ravi: Is there a recommended approach for secrets management for per-tenant keys so we don't store raw Redwood keys in our DB?
[09:46] Priya: Best practice: store tenant-to-key mapping in a secure secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) and have the gateway fetch ephemeral tokens or do key exchange. We can help with a design pattern doc.
[09:58] Marta: For observability we want request-level traces joined with our transaction IDs. Is it as simple as propagating x-trace-id?
[10:04] Ethan: Yes, propagate trace headers; Redwood will surface those values in the console and you can correlate via the tracing export. There are also built-in alerts and token-level cost breakouts.
[10:18] Liam: Slightly nitty: do you enforce tokenization differences? We use a custom tokenizer for some pre-processing.
[10:24] Priya: You can pre-tokenize on your side; Redwood charges are based on canonical tokenization for the model, but you can pre-process to reduce payload size — we'll document the recommended approach.
[10:40] Ravi: Ok, let's summarize action owners.
[10:44] Ava: (recap) Ava: pricing & SOW; Ethan: code + gateway repo + LangChain/LlamaIndex examples + OpenTelemetry collector sample; Priya: security docs; Hypernova: prompts + network info.
[10:59] Marta: Sounds good. We'll aim for the POC in two weeks and follow up on the infra deep-dive.
[11:06] Ava: Thanks all — we'll send links in the next 24 hours.
[11:10] Ravi: Thanks everyone.
[11:12] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has light ASR errors in product names and acronyms (e.g., 'KV cacha' instead of KV cache). Links shared during call: [redwood/dedicated-pricing.pdf], [github.com/redwood/gateway-example], [docs.redwood/langchain-llamaindex-snippets].
